items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: All except one, Mrs. Clark. I'll never forget, she told me, she said...

ctx.x: studying, but I would come up with those good report cards because I could remember, you know. If I'd hear them say something, you know... I had a good memory. So I was very good in school. In fact, when I got... In fact, I was in the sixth grade, and all of my teachers agreed to let me skip Seven and Eight, and go to the Ninth Grade. All except one, Mrs. Clark. I'll never forget, she told me, she said... "Look," she said, "don't think I'm holding you back, but if you do this, you're going to miss too much, and…

But I was well-known around through Jackson, you know, and I had... We had staged some dances, the kids at school, we had... When we graduated from the Ninth Grade, we staged some dances and stuff, you know, and had the band playing down there. Our principal at the school, boy, that would be the last thing he'd want to see happen, but we had all of the teachers going for it, so we won him over, after it all happened, you know. He didn't know until it was all over. But he came on in with us, you know.
